newsitem.title: USA: Kodak looking to boost Advantix.
newsitem.headline: Kodak looking to boost Advantix.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co President Dan Carp said Thursday the company plans to spend $100 million on advertising for its Advantix camera after it "lost some momentum" in last year's premiere.
"Now, we're out to get that momentum back," Carp said after the company's annual presentation to analysts and media.
Last year, the company spent about $65 million on advertising to launch the product.
But Advantix, an Advanced Photo System camera that uses traditional film with digital enhancements, was hampered by production problems that stalled its entry into the retail arena, Carp said.

It also was held back by photo developers, particularly mini photo labs, that were not geared up to handle the new product and told customers they would need to ship their film to Kodak for developing, and by some retailers who did not want to take the time to explain a new system, industry analysts said.

"The APS program was flawed (industrywide) in its launch because of lack of availability of cameras. But it is not a flawed product," Prudential Securities analyst Alex Henderson told reporters after the meeting. "It will become the dominant film system over time. This is clearly a superior product, no question about it."

Industrywide, four million Advanced Photo System cameras were sold last year, while 14 milion APS film cassettes were sold, Carp said. In 1997, Kodak expects the industry to sell 11 million APS cameras and 70 million film cassettes.
The company would not say what its share of the APS market was in 1996 or what it projects its share will be in 1997.
"It's really early to see how that's going to settle out," Carp said after the media presentation.
Analysts said they thought Kodak would actually end up spending more on advertising for Advantix in 1997 than the $100 million announced on Thursday.

Smith Barney analyst Peter Enderlin said he was pleased because he thought Kodak would end up spending $100 million above its 1996 Advantix advertising budget, taking the total expenditure this year $165 million.
"That's actually a plus," Enderlin said. "I do think they'll be able to get the awareness up."
((-- Lisa Marie Pane, New York newsdesk 212-859-1713))
